column1: # Canonical source ownership for the bounded connected warning-to-protocol runtime.

column5: The bounded runtime makes the mutex-protected StaticWarningHandler the sole warning store owned by StatementStatus and delegates reset, capped single append, source batch-cap behavior, set, snapshot, total count, and Error count. Warning/Note/Error levels, copy with capacity reuse, independent truncation, message JSON round trips, and Go-compatible wrapping uint16 publication remain source-shaped. Typed terror.Error JSON identity, generic wrapped-error cause recovery, arbitrary custom level strings, Go nil-slice identity, zero-copy GetWarnings, funcWarnAppender, and SHOW WARNINGS remain open.

The bounded runtime connects begin/finish, retry reset, row counters, last-insert-ID, message, ExecSuccess, and the owned StaticWarningHandler in one direct Go-shaped StatementStatus. Finish snapshots ordered warnings once into immutable PublishedStatementStatus, and total/error counts wrap through uint16 rather than saturating. The same source also backs existing reserved-row-ID, pushdown-flag, refcount, used-stats, stats-load-result, alternative-plan, chunk-allocation, and SET_VAR restore leaves; full EvalContext, SQL mode, error context, every warning producer, full SessionVars, storage reservation, worker/retry orchestration, planner rounds, chunk-pool lifecycle, hint parsing/mutation/restoration, and real session ownership remain open.

The first five read-only/no-op registrations preserve canonical names, aliases, scopes, offline-mode distinction, and checkReadOnly ON/1 OFF/ON/WARN policy; the remaining noopSysVars registry, SysVar validation plumbing, SessionVars mutation, and global accessor lifecycle remain external.

The bounded runtime keeps the isolation enum/capability and option-value conversions explicit while checkReadOnly's session WARN branch appends to the live Session StatementStatus-owned StaticWarningHandler for ordered reset, one-time snapshot, and wrapping count publication through COM_QUERY. tidb_skip_isolation_level_check warnings, other SysVar validation, error-code identity, global access, and generic SessionVars plumbing remain open.
